doc.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Mother Rose and the Barbarin family of drummers
summary: His mother came from the large Barbarin family; her brothers Paul, Willie, Lucien and Louis played music as extra income and status.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My mother was named Rose. She was of the Barbarin family. It was a huge family, Barbarins. My mother had, what?, four sisters and . . . four brothers and four sisters . . . four brothers and five sisters.
The Barbarin family is one of the most popular names in New Orleans music with names like Paul and Louis and Isidore. How is your mother related to them?

That’s her brothers you call. Paul’s a brother. Willie’s a brother. Lucien’s a brother. Paul, Willie, Lucien, and Louis. They all played music, because my whole family . . . We were encouraged to play music, because it added to the poor folk’s moneybag. It added a little money more to the . . . You played as a extra to your regular job, whatever you . . . was your profession or your trade. Mostly your trade. By playing music, you added on weekends or anytime, you added to the moneybags in the family.
So it was an honor to be a musician.

It was a honor because you were celebrated. Every . . . all kids wants to be celebrated. He wants to be noticed when he walk the street. That’s why they nickname kids after movie stars and football stars. Give them some kind of identification that he’s somebody. So that is that. She had four brothers and four sisters [Barker repeats this, sounding unsure].
